tagline: Down Route 100 through ski country to Coolidge's notch.
intro: This stretch of Vermont 100 runs south from Pittsfield, mountain grazing country where 19th-century humorists said the one-legged milking stool was invented, through Killington and Plymouth to Ludlow. A branch, Route 100A, runs about seven miles northeast past Plymouth Notch to US 4 in Bridgewater.
The Killington and Okemo ski areas lie on or near the road, but most of the way it keeps a rural feel.

moments.title: Killington
moments.text: Called Sherburne until it took back its old name in 1999, the ski town has twice voted to leave Vermont for New Hampshire, a largely symbolic gesture.

moments.title: Coolidge Homestead
moments.text: In the family parlor here Calvin Coolidge was sworn in as president by his father, who refused to modernize the house, so it still looks much as it did that night.

moments.title: Ludlow
moments.text: Calvin Coolidge went to school here at Black River Academy, and the village's woolen mill was rebuilt in brick at three stories after the first one burned in 1865.
